newsitem.title: INDIA: Fifteen wounded in grenade attack on Kashmir leader.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen wounded in grenade attack on Kashmir leader.

text.p: Suspected separatist guerrillas exploded a hand grenade at an election rally being addressed by Kashmiri leader Farooq Abdullah on Monday, wounding 15 people, police said.

They said Abdullah escaped unhurt in the attack at Kishtwar, some 240 km (150 miles) east of Jammu, the winter capital of the troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir. It was the second attack on Abdullah during a month-long poll campaign.
Police said the grenade exploded before militants could hurl it into area where Abdullah was speaking. Three of the wounded were in serious condition. No other details were immediately available.
Abdullah, chief of Kashmir's biggest political party, the National Conference, was speaking during the four-phase local polls being held in the state.
The polls are the first in the state in nine years, and come six years after the outbreak of a separatist revolt in 1990. September 30 is the last day of the poll.

More than 20,000 people have been killed during the separatist revolt in mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state. New Delhi put the restive state under direct federal rule at the start of the separatist uprising six years ago.
